correctness.rationale: In either sparse power set P={b^i:i>=0} for b=d>=2 or b=t, the restricted multiplication graph R(b^i,b^j,b^k) holds exactly when k=i+j. Thus x != y and exists z in P with R(x,z,y) defines i<j on powers and has the order property, proving instability. The Hawthorne NIP theorems (integer all d>=2 and polynomial prime p>=7) are confirmed in the primary PDFs. Domain and orientation are correct; the issue is prior coverage, not correctness.
